reviews.text: I'm really exited about this game, I randomly came across it today and as soon as I read what the game was I sat refreshing steam until I was able to buy and play it. I've barely scratched the surface, but from what I have played has already convinced me I will spend HOURS in this game. I'm already creating my custom harem xD (I know for shame, but I care not). This feels like Elona but in 2024, way more comprehensible and less overwhelming. The translation from what I've read is really good, the odd thing here and there but that's to be expected. But it's comprehensible, and at no point have I felt I misunderstood a mechanic. Considering the Dev is not a native English speaker and this was outsourced for translation, their cooperation seems to have been thorough. Also, I love the tutorial, I feel like i'm having a conversation with kuetaro, it was a quaint and charming touch i don't normally feel in Video Games, so well done :) Edit: This game is in dire need of a compare feature for equipment and such. Definitely something that I would like to see included in the game, unless I have totally miss it's inclusion. I would LOVE to see an easy way to make sprites for this game? I think if the Dev could make a software kit for creating the PNG's and add it to the game that would be just... well immense. That's just wishlist stuff though and not important. A fun and ambitious game from a solo dev, and I would LOVE to see what they would be able to create with decent financial backing and a team. For the scope of this game, and the clear love and attention put into it, it's well worth the price-tag. Anime/JRPG/Sandbox and Isekai lovers paradise game. Arigato Gozaimasu keureto-san.

Alright I wanted to wait until I got a little bit further in understanding the game to make a review. Of course I'm only 8 hours in so I'm far less further in the game then I'm sure other's are. I see a 0.1% of folk above lvl 50 and lvl 100 so hah! Best way I can describe this game is that it's an rpg game with a feeling of Etrian mystery dungeon stylish combat although not exactly. What's impressive is that you are set up in a way to make your own story experience and proceed through the world how you want. I'll do a quick break down. Somehow you are the creator of your world, it's pure randomized locations and people, skills and environments. You can change settings such as the male to female ratio, as well as % of npc's as criminals. In playing the game you can play it like a rune factory game, interact with people every little bit to gain relation, can learn to farm and blacksmith. But there's an adventuring guild where you can gain missions, everything from basic procurement to Hey there's an army of monsters coming we need your help. What I love about this game is that I feel like I'm the creator of a world coming down and helping everywhere I can. I'm an adventurer, i'm spending time with people, I found an academy for example and upon entering I befriended some students and faculty and ended up making a group out of them. We've gone to a dungeon, camped together and ate, hell I ended up starting a relationship with one a few minutes ago. In essence the game is designed in a way for you to play in a world that's got it's own people doing things as they can. It won't look like a game where you see people leave town and travel somewhere, but you can 100% run into someone from a town who asks for help getting back to it. I died and failed a couple times early on and was downgraded to "Punk" haha. There's just a lot more to this game then you'd think. Get past the idea of okay folk are standing about, don't think oh they don't say much. Take it a bit at a time, talk to people, understand the systems and feel like it's not a player but yourself in the game helping people (or attacking folk and being a criminal since can do that) I'll try and make a better review, little less wordy once I make more progress. But it's a game that you'll know you love if you've ever been like "Damn I always wanted to have a game where I could feel like i'm in the world and advancing little by little"

[h1]tl;dr Summary[/h1] If you enjoyed Castle of the Wind (I'm old I know), Izuna, Mystery Dungeon, or Elona then this game will be something you want to at least check out. It's not perfect, but it is gamepad compatible and it's got a lot of things you'll love. If not, your mileage may vary so nab the demo. Just bear in mind, this is an open-ended roguelike, so you'll want to visit ingame locations if you're the sort of person who needs objectives. It'll give you more than enough. [h2]What it is[/h2] Creator of Another World is a roguelike much in the same vein as Elona 2014 (The not-rip-off one), but fans of Castle of the Wind or similar games from the early 90's will feel very much at home. Fans of Izuna will like it, but there are a few caveats we'll get to later. Entirely "Turn-based" in that unmistakable "Roguelike" way, you can - from what I've seen so far - opt to live your life in a wide variety of manners. Dungeon delver? Sure. Chef? Why not. Murderous rampage? I mean... You do you, buddy. Like these, you're given enough information to start off, but the further you dig deeper the more there are a variety of mechanics which you can sink your teeth in to. Fortunately, the game doesn't fall in the trap of expecting you to learn everything right off the bat and you can muddle your way through fine early on (Looking at you, Dungeons of Dredmor). Arcane unexplained mechanics don't stop there; There's a "war" feature for some quests akin to Suikoden. You'll want to learn War Tactics from the Adventurer's Guild for that. There's a casino. There's fishing. There's *stuff* and I probably haven't seen half of it. The best bit is you can ignore or engage in as much or as little of the content as possible. [h2]What Does it Do Well?[/h2] When it comes to it's [i]roguelike[/i] credentials, It hits all the satisfying beats many come to expect:[list] [*]> You walk and explore randomly generated tilemaps, towns, dungeons, and so on. [*]> You can discover items and weaponry, much of it needing identifying. [*]> Dungeon delving! [*]> Skills to learn, scrolls to use, explore as you go. [/list] When it comes to [i]Elona[/i]-esque features, you can be satisfied that:[list] [*]> There are a wide variety of procedurally generated characters to interact with. [*]> You can, indeed, partake in the world in other ways such as fishing, gambling, murderous intent. [*]> You can befriend plenty of people. [*]> Procedural questing is [i]very[/i] well sign-posted, with characters going "Damn that's a problem" as you walk into a town, and an adventurers board which has plenty of stuff to signpost your exploration. [/list] As for the more general stuff:[list] [*]> The tutorial does a genuinely good job of going through the basics. [*]> There [i][b]is[/b][/i] a main plot, but you'll have to do a little exploring and check any [i]red text[/i] you come across to uncover the Main Story Quests. [*]> There's enough base character customisation to enjoy, and [i]the game doesn't tell you, but if you press confirm on the portrait or NPC walking preview you can see a much more user-friendly table of them[/i]... More on that later in the bad side though. [*]> World customisation is... Interesting. Not that I'm fussed, but you can absolutely customise an all male/female world if you want, have custom adventurers come in and out of your world as they retire (Ew) and so on. [*]> There is definitely a lot of scope for modding, with an in-game browser for portraits, walking animations, ally dialogue(!), and more. [*]> You have a lot of stats and stuff you can fiddle with or not at your leisure. [*]> Side content, including fishing, gambling, and just generally being at one with the world, is pretty good. [*]> If you like content with no set goal and a persistent, everlasting world then this is your bag. It does have a Main Story, but you need to pay attention to come across it. [/list] I actually kinda want to really reiterate this though: [b[ The procedural questing is actually quite refreshing in how it's handled and the variety.[/b] It's decently executed, doesn't happen so constantly it's in the way, isn't rammed down your throat, but is definitely sign-posted and very visible if you want or need it. You definitely won't get bored. [h2]What Does it Do Badly?[/h2] Again, bullet point list because I like them:[list] [*]> Character creation is horribly inconsistent. Like terribly. There are portraits for NPC's which have no correlation to the walking animations and vice-versa. [i]I am not saying that the portraits are AI generated, but they are definitely very inconsistent[/i] [*]> The UI is kinda sign-posted, but also a lot not. Ew. It makes navigating what you want to do ingame 60% okay, 40% not. [*]> The translation. Hoo-boy. I volunteer myself to help, because oh heavens it needs some work. [*]> Some of the mechanics are [i]extremely arcane[/i] or are very much "[i]well we've thrown you in, have fun having no idea that you needed to prep first[/i]" (Looking at you, Suikoden war mechanic) [*]> Menus could do with a bit of work, as could resolution/zoom information. I feel someone really needs to change how they do window resizing and the like, it took me a good few minutes to make the game squint-free. [*]> There is no option to zoom in/zoom out in-game. This is AWFUL for navigation sometimes or when things get busy. [*]> No easy way to compare items. More a bug-bear, but given every item can have an inordinate amount of modifications it's kinda really a big thing. [*]> Some of the UI is big. Some is small. Some things are obscure, some are not (e.g. You can't hand an item directly from your inventory to a party member, you have to "give" it to them... But if you want to take it, you have to go into their inventory and take it). [*]> Some quality of life stuff is missing, including: - Better control over what party members do/don't use, especially when they're prone to blowing big stuff quickly or skill books when they have no business doing so) - You can't equip party members from your own inventory, or use skill books on them from your own inventory either. - Controller issues, but they're not a big deal honestly. [/list] [h2]So... Play it?[/h2] If you like the genre, absolutely. Despite what's missing, what's rough around the edges, and what's questionable, this is probably the best in the genre for years. It's not as polished as a Mystery Dungeon, but it's a lot more fun overall. It's not as fun as an Izuna, but it's got a lot more content. It's definitely no Castle of the Wind... But that's a good thing, because it can offer you so much more. If you [i]don't[/i] like the genre, absolutely not. This isn't one of those genre-busting games. If you [i]don't know[/i] then I strongly recommend you play the demo. It's gonna be a Marmite, you will either love it or hate it. Give it 90 minutes (including tutorial time) and you should know how you feel about it. [h2]Anything else?[/h2] This really [i]does need a lot more work done to smooth it out[/i] and I'm not going to lie to you and pretend it doesn't. It does. The gameplay is doing all the heavy lifting, simply because it's so good. One thing which would help is the addition of Steam Workshop compatibility, but I dare say because it has its own in-game version we won't get that. It would [i]really[/i] help though, given how lacklustre the in-game browser is. But yeah, hope that helps you make a decision! Feel free to leave a comment if you have any questions.

This isn't a bad game. This is actually a pretty good game, maybe even a very good game. But the fundamental problem with this game is that this game is basically just Elona in RPGMaker - I haven't really seen anything that screams "This is like Elona, but different" as opposed to "This is just Elona with a bit less polish, that I have to relearn" other than the weird world creation mechanic that imo doesn't really add anything to the game. It may be mechanically less complex, but it's not mechanically less complex *enough*, and at the end of the day, you're paying 15 dollars (and in 10 days 19 dollars) for a somewhat worse version of a game that already exists (its important to remember that Elona is still being updated and forked) that you can get for free. And I can't recommend a game that immediately made me want to play a *different* game.

**Some spoilers** Its a Roguelike that plays like a mashup of a Final Fantasy / Dungeons and Dragons game. You make your character, can recruit up to a party of 5. ( 3 at start. ) From the moment you start the game you have free reign to do whatever you want. Want to be a noble hero who does quests killing monsters for the local towns? You can do that. Want to be a dastardly thief who steals everything, or worse kills everything you can? You can do that. Want to be a farmer/fisherman who supplies food for the towns? You can do that. In fact, you can do all of them at the same time in the same playthrough. Early on you will have some inventory issues as you want/need to collect everything you find on the ground; but with enough time and adventuring experience you get some DnD like bags of holding for holding cooking ingredients, finished meals, and alchemy ingredients. ( They weigh 5 each but you will be carrying more than that in weight anytime you go into a new area and start collecting. ) The game creator is Japanese and outsourced the English translation. Overall its pretty good and very readable, occasional spelling mistakes but nothing so bad that you cant figure out. Weapons/Armor/Accessories can have a variety of affixes/bonuses/negatives that make each item that drops unique and you will have to figure out what you want and what you need. Upgrades will come eventually and you will have to look at every piece individually to weigh if it is something you want to equip or give to your party members. ( The number at the end [ 0.6, 1.2, etc ] is its general item level, the quality [ poor, average, Exceptional, Best, etc ] combined together with the item level will give you a quick glance at how good something is. The individual stats on the item may be better or worse than something already equipped. There is not currently a 'compare' screen so you must manually look at each piece and flip between to see what changes and what you want. Early on upgrades are straightforward, you start with trash starting adventurer gear and almost any Exceptional piece will be better for a given slot. Once you get a bit further in you will have more options for stat upgrades and your choices become a bit harder. Remember that this is a Roguelike. If your main character dies that file is over. You will want a Monk as a Healer but everything is very fluid and how you want to play. There are books that will drop to train new skills and abilities, so with enough time any character can probably do anything but the characters stats will determine how good they are at it. In your party you may also want a Rogue for opening locked things and a melee acting as a tank to keep attacks off of your casters; but again the game is very fluid and you may be able to run 5 casters and simply overpower everything you encounter. I wouldnt recommend it but you have the freedom to do it. There is a relationship system that I have not had much experience with yet. Everyone you meet at first will be Ignore and be standoffish, but with enough time talking and getting to know people and giving gifts the relationships will improve and you will be able to invite people to your party. I have very little experience with this so far but apparently you can have lovers and have children. For a first release the game is very stable, I have encountered 0 bugs and 0 errors. It could use some polishing and modern features like the equipment compare screen, but as is is very playable and fun. The author is active online and reads Reddit and replies to people suggesting things so I expect we will see updates in the future that expand the current gameplay further. ( People were suggesting harder difficulty mode options and they seemed receptive and interested so we will see what comes ) Overall, a good game, a great initial release. If you are interested in a freeform Roguelike where you have a party of adventurers who go on Dungeons and Dragons, you will enjoy this game. I am not far enough in to speak to its depth and mid/lategame, but I am having fun and am enjoying the experience so far.

Finished all postgame dungeons on a pure solo character. Very comfy game! As the introduction on storefront says, it is a casual game with low difficulty. So if you're looking for an open world roguelike with high difficulty, like in Cataclysm, UnReal World, ADOM, or like in some Angband variants, you won't find it here. With that said, the game offers an anime sandbox-y that is clearly inspired by Elona and its variants (play those games please). Where Creators of Another World differs is in how it de-fangs some "less casual player friendly" aspects of its inspiration. A forgiving hunger mechanic, straightforward character building with some depth and significantly simpler ways to go about growing in power (no potentials, plat coins, etc.), less instant kills and surprises in general. Featuring a good amount of freedom in how you make your own story in the world. Fish your way into cooking food for your party, farm and sell your crops, marry and have children... or conquer dungeons instead with its nice combat design! If you liked Elona and its variants and then wanted some more, I highly recommend this game.

There still are events and encounters but it's not as chaotic and unhinged, for better or for worse. Detracting a point because fourteen Euros is too much even on sale, and adding a point because it plays like a video game.

A fun blend of genres that results in a particularly unusual and interesting game: a roguelike that feels more like an RPG than most roguelikes do. The themes are varied, and there's a bunch of unexpected little mini-games sprinkled throughout the world you're creating. Being able to create a town of your character's friends and even outfit it with working shops and services is a personal favorite feature. A close second is the content-import features: it's very easy to add sprites or portraits to your game, they sync with steam cloud, and there's an online downloader for content others have uploaded. Creator is significantly different than other similar games in its genre despite any initial similarities. The stand-out differences are that you can form a strong, coherent party and that the party members contribute (often massively) toward surviving combat - in other roguelikes, party members are of questionable utility outside of specific, game-breaking usages. Creator is more balanced in this regard. XP and gold rewards are mostly split between party members, so the slimmer your team, the faster you'll grow. Early on I relied on having a full party to progress, and toward the late game I moved around solo more to rapidly gain power for the climax. It's fun how both methods are rewarded, and this is one of the ways in which it feels more like a conventional RPG. Roguelike purists might balk at a few of its nonstandard features, such as the lack of permadeath and ability to load your saved game at will, but these things mostly contribute to the game's comfort and playability: unlike most roguelikes, Creator feels like it wants to challenge you but ultimately it feels like it wants you to succeed. The game's content is more intended for a long-form single playthrough, as opposed to the roguelikes that rely on continually restarting the player's progress to make them replayable. If you're totally new to the type of game the challenge will be significantly greater. Since the game is open-ended however, there's a variety of ways to become stronger or deal with difficulties. For instance: it's feasible to deal with a dungeon that causes status effects or a boss with instakill spells either by acquiring items to protect against these things or through brute-force, raw-power methods. I played it about half the time on the Steam Deck, and the controls for this are quite good for the genre. I hadn't actually intended to ever play a top-down roguelike on the deck, but it was surprisingly comfortable. I also played briefly on Windows and the rest of the time on Linux; there were no particular issues, although Linux isn't officially supported. I was about 64 hours in when I finished the main quest but I'm guessing that I play games like this at a significantly more relaxed pace than others: maybe 20-30 for most players. There's a bunch of optional postgame content to drive that up even further, and by this point I still haven't dug into multiple game features, like farming, and I've yet to make several of the facilities. It's fun. You can probably tell whether or not you want this kind of game from the previews and description, but if you're on the fence the demo might be worth grabbing first.

I really wish steam had a neutral rating, as I'm planning to follow this game and possibly repurchase it in the future once I feel more quality of life and stability features are implemented. The core concept is good, you are the creator of your own world, and in this, you have entered it with a limited power, able to live and work in it, save people, help people, succeed, fail, make friends, enemies, forge and craft, all the good stuff. However, its buggy, first play through I'd really expected some level of auto-save on screen transitions if all the bugs WEREN'T worked out. That's a standard feature. Some fast way to hide the damage and messages section is standard in games like this, but wasn't apparent or obvious if it existed. There's also no way to eat a stack of food without assigning it to a hot key. So how did this come to a refund and a no rating just from that? First run through I tackle a few dungeons, the difficulty level is DECIDEDLY easy, as it should be, so saving really, truly is more to ensure progress isn't lost. I get to the "storage statue" in the first town, store some items.... and my item selection screen goes blank.... I can't exit, can't save, and had to alt-tab out and close it. As I did this, I even thought (maybe from years of playing Elona varients and other roguelikes?) that surely a save file was no more than 10 minutes old, or one screen transition, and all I was losing was a few minutes of time and progress.... that wasn't the case. 1hr, 20 minutes gone, in a blink. Now maybe some people go to the menu, and dig around for the save feature that isn't exactly easy to find every few minutes, and maybe this random bug will happen to one out of every 1,000 people and can't be reproduced, but for me it was a big sign that this is more early access at what I'd expect to be full price for this style, quality, and nature of a game. Is the game bad? No it's actually pretty good, but when the technical limitations and difficulties outweigh the quality of the game, you really start to wish there was a star ratting on Steam. If I had to give it a direct rating in stars, it would be 2.5 out of 5, not enough to not refund, and enough that I'm hoping in the future big changes will cause me to want to purchase it again and give it another go. Thing is, you don't keep nearly a $20 game on steam when dozens of games in that price range have less bugs, or have at least the early access tag on them to show they are, in fact early access. Hoping the dev makes some changes, and we see something amazing out of this. There are 3 - 4 games that capture the spirit of this kind of thing, and this is the only one that isn't an Elona Variant right now. That said, almost $20 isn't a good price point for something where it will be a "wait and hope the developer implements all these quality of life features that are necessary to ensure playability till bugs are worked out." Hopeful to be able to change my review in the future. If you can handle the issues I just mentioned definitely go for it, if not, keep your eyes peeled on it, maybe the dev will get a combination of bug fixes and stability QoL features that ease this kind of situation. Edit: So why did I change the rating and repurchase? I really do see a lot of potential in this game, and would like to support the developer. I feel like, sometimes 2hrs isn't enough of a window for games like this, and it forces a "refund if you are unsure" situation. Especially with crashes at an hour mark. I'm going to give this a try with the unofficial quick save mod, and worst case scenario will update this review again.

elin出来前的elona唯一代餐，前期比elona好上手得多，中期感觉词条、技能、特性的缺乏使得战斗和刷宝体验比较无聊，其他钓鱼、种田、赌博、迷宫（那个活动的3d迷宫，好像还奖励收纳技能书）系统做得比较简陋，肉鸽元素也没有在借鉴elona的前提下创新多少，导致步入后期的动力不太充足，不过因为是唯一代餐所以该玩还得玩 新手建议：1.过完教程之后在初始之地，先在左边雕像捏两个队友，算上主角一共三个人，最好包含一个僧侣、一个魔法输出（魔法战士、巫师、魔法师等）、一个用来当前排肉盾的近战，这样足够应对全时期的战斗了，不过队伍上限5人，因为会分得任务奖励的钱，可以等不缺钱以后再招点喜欢的角色 2.初始之地下边的雕像可以学减少地图移动时间的本领，有花1个认识度和2个认识度的，后者走一格大概20分钟，酌情选择购买时机 3.新手村跟npc都对话一遍，会发现有的npc满足条件能教本领，有的可以用8个辉石换收纳袋，素材收纳袋要尽早入手，用来装锻造冶炼用的材料等，属于从一开始就需要积累的 4.第一次拓展世界前最好存档，拓展之后务必看下有没有出沙漠，沙漠是出赌场的必要地形，如果没有沙漠的话第二次拓展就不会出赌场，会再往后拖，而赌场里能轻易获取高rank的戒指、剑盾、其他一些必要物品，很有必要刷出来 5.开荒阶段刷认知度最快的方法是走主线迷宫，地图上有个event的迷宫就是了，打完送1认知度（印象中是这样） 6.这之后想刷辉石认知度等，推荐在城镇把歼灭一群敌人的任务全部接了，然后出去清掉，这个跟讨伐的区别是讨伐要打完某个n层迷宫最后的boss，而歼灭只需要进一个只有一层的临时迷宫

7/10 This game is quite similar to Elona, but everything will be procedurally generated including towns and world. This is the good point for me. Below are bad points: 1. 更适合老滚玩家的elona。 elona的恶意设定太多，再加上玩家群体的特点，道德底线高的玩家玩起来太难受了。 异世界创造者的底子虽然是类elona的，但在游玩风格上更接近打了mod的老滚：犯罪会被卫兵打，可以（免费）雇佣你见到的大部分NPC（这个是老滚mod的效果），可以锻造出毁天灭地级别的装备。总之是鼓励你一边种田一边遵纪守法的，可以安安心心过日子。 而且这游戏即使是特殊NPC（功能性NPC，剧情NPC，女神等）也都能招募和结婚（好像唯一例外是国王），各种小怪也都能捕获成队友，能做到这一点的游戏屈指可数，让我举例子的话我只知道一个命中注定召唤术。而且招募之后可以任意修改队友的AI和装备（比如禁止队友捡某些类型的物品，更改战斗风格，禁止队友自己换装备等），这一点基本比所有游戏都强了，像老滚里我给队友塞的神装动不动就消失属实让人吐血，而这游戏里通过改AI+塞神装+塞技能书可以让任何队友成为战神，只要你肯把足够多的资源给ta。（PS：其实这样培养之后会发现很多平民职业NPC同等级下不比战斗职业差，因为所有人的成长率总和都基本一样） 当前版本的各种功能也比较贴心，比如可以直接一键解咒放在道具袋里的道具。 缺点：1、任务失败会扣很多道德，不太合理。2.某些情况没考虑全，比如不走剧情硬打死奴延之后会无事发生，连奖励都不掉，主要是作者都没想到有玩家能靠正常游戏手段打死。 硬打奴延挺刺激的，不暴击的话伤害全是1而且奴延每回合回1600多血，连某个怪鸟都不配给奴延提鞋。

惊为天人！找了这么多年，终于找到了。 8月2号偶然间在steam看到这个游戏的简介，短短几行字就吸引了我的注意，然后看了销售页面详细的游戏介绍，然后毫不犹豫原价付款了。 怎么说呢，我很早以前就想玩一款集RPG、冒险、养成、经营、种田、休闲于一体的游戏，自从30岁以后就彻底不想玩那种PVP的类型了，找了好久，老滚5好玩儿吧，但是我嫌弃他自由度不够高，传统rpg类型，后来出了个蹩脚的生存模式也没感觉，音乐也不好听。骑砍好玩儿吧，但是我嫌弃他不能种地建造，剧情也几乎没有，音乐也不好听。英灵神殿威尔海姆好玩儿吧，但是我嫌他满世界就我一个人，没有NPC，没有城镇，没有烟火气，操作也怪怪的，背景音乐也不够好。怪猎好玩儿吧，我4000多小时了，操作打击感一流，但是我还是嫌弃不能种地不能养老，没有生活气息，背景音乐倒是很带感。之前有好多缝合怪都有这些元素的影子，比如创世理想乡、帕鲁等，但是感觉都缝的很蹩脚，不够，严重不够。 我一度已经放弃要那么多元素都能集合到一起的游戏了，因为我觉得我的要求很苛刻，对程序员们应该会是一个折磨，要做到全部凑一起还没bug的，我觉得不太可能。之前我还在一款游戏里评论写了：括号内是该评论复制（真的很奇怪，目前还真的没有哪个RPG游戏是这个游戏里面冒险者们做的事。我就想找一款RPG或者ARPG类的游戏，自己出去打怪爆材料，回城里打装备或者卖掉赚钱，赚的钱用来生活、买家具、买房子、买地建房子、开一块地种点药材或者种点菜，系统再刷点随机高难度任务或者阵营冲突，多好啊，为什么没有人做呢，是因为程序太难写了吗？还是这种不适合当今快餐文化横行的游戏模式？）有人还留言给我推荐恶意不息，还以为是我想要的类型，结果买了玩儿了两个小时赶紧退款，恶心的要命的一游戏，完全和我写的不搭边。 在这个游戏之前玩儿的是一款修仙类游戏，我已经觉得应该是找到算是最符合我喜好的类型了，音乐好听，文本量也够，当小说看，沉浸感也足，我给了目前为止10年steam游戏里的最高评价，我认为是目前同类型最好的，短短几天就上百小时了，但是缺点就是通了就没了，彻底玩两遍剧情以后，发觉足够的细节以后就没激情了，因为不够长，我的评论也是觉得不够。 然后突然有一天，在steam商店首页往下翻的推荐里因为我玩儿了上面的那个修仙游戏，出现了这个，4月底出的游戏我竟然错过了，而且都不知道它的存在，直到前天，这是多么符合我的要求啊，RPG，冒险者公会，接任务，打怪赚钱，剑与魔法的世界，城市，自建城镇，好友度，自建角色，自建NPC角色，2B国王，2B王子，勇者，女神，角色养成，种田，烹饪，饱食度，锻造，制药，甚至还可以抓怪当宠物（虽然我没抓过），音乐很好听，剧情虽有些俗套（估计是近几年2B坏女神动漫套路太多了，有点儿审美疲劳），自由度和游戏元素可以说覆盖非常全面。甚至可以一夫多妻一妇多夫，甚至还可以一夫多夫。 啊！！！！不行，想夸的太多了，我目前也就到40级而已，只是个新人冒险者带了俩小哥闯世界，先来评论了，真要写，估计写一篇几万字论文都写不完，总之就是，大赞！一万个赞！十万个赞！

Although this game is often compared to Elona there are some things it does better than Elona, although it's nowhere near as content filled as Elona. Map encounters having chances to result in impromptu quests of a variety of sorts Map encounters resulting in a variety of events. Music tracks: there are some refreshing low-fi and even some surprisingly dark even sci-fi feeling tracks. Usable skills being learned from books and there being shops for them makes the skill system much more cohesive. Making the world feel populated with adventurers; you are far more likely to encounter other adventurers adventuring instead of it being a news ticker. However oddly they don't seem to actually achieve anything in terms of completing quests or conquering dungeons I see this as a negative. They are often present in even generic events that happen throughout the world. Dialogue wise, they all seem to have some kind of selected personality/dialogue lines. They seem simple but have enough flavor to make them feel all not the same. Procedural Generated Places and Towns making your world a bit more unique to you. I feel the game needs more content and items. The creator is active in the discussions but it doesn't feel like there are any plans for any major updates. We will be lucky to get whatever we get. It would be interesting if a game like this had workshop content. unfortunately there is no workshop support for this game currently. I feel like it needs some QOL improvements in some areas, the way turns are processed could use some adjustment, holding down that key for the speed up makes it jittery, and it only then feels at normal speed. The unheld speed could use a bit of speed up. If this game added much more content and dived even deeper into the protagonists power I could see myself sinking thousands of hours into this game.

This is good. No, this is very good. Summoned in another world with a choice of jobs and there are magic and monsters. There are several abilities to help daily life such as elemental understanding, cooking, trading, natural recovery and others. Unlike abilities that continue to be added without limits and high upgrades, skills have a capacity limit of 10 with limited proficiency and different levels. The jobs that have been offered at the beginning are indeed varied, but I think it is still lacking. I hope in the future there will also be non-combat jobs such as tamer, slave trader, leader and others. What is good here in my opinion is freedom. Yes! freedom! You can do good deeds and get good jobs and reputation. Do normal jobs, hunt monsters, deliver goods, give gifts to people and join in the attack. For the last one, I think there are still many shortcomings. If you can organize ranks, add troops and be more free to use strategies, I think it could be better. In addition, you can also do bad things such as murder and theft and enter a dark guild to get bad jobs. If you find a bad city, besides offering bad jobs, the items sold are also different from normal cities. Of course the items are suitable for doing bad things. It should be noted, if you accept work from a dark guild or people in the city, your reputation will also worsen even though the task you take is limited to eradicating monsters. Relationships with people (including animals) are also needed here. Sometimes some of them also offer abilities with several conditions. At least this can reduce the expenditure of one of your currencies to buy abilities. Well, you can also marry those who are even different species / have the same gender. Of course you can marry many people and make a harem. The last thing I want to discuss is the city. The city is a source of good meetings with people or supplies. Although there are luxurious cities, I think the land is still limited, so the existing npc and facilities are also limited. I hope that in the future the size of the city can be more varied and the goods sold are also of better quality than cities / villages with lower quality. For cities built by players themselves, I hope they can also be expanded with certain conditions such as banners or certificates. I think it's long enough so that's it. For the story, I haven't finished it so I can't give my impression. In conclusion, this game is very amazing and works it for that price. Don't hesitate to buy it and I really recommend it. 100/10

像素风游戏玩了不少，但是每一款基本上都只在自己侧重的领域有可玩内容。这款名字看起来平平无奇的，反而面面俱到，在自由度，可玩性和难易度上达到了很好的平衡。 这游戏在沙盒开放世界下，支线和角色剧情整的挺好，诙谐幽默还玩梗。至于整体设定，职业，装备，锻造，炼金，钓鱼，种地，买卖，打怪，升级，攻略，结婚，生子......真的是包含了异世界穿越的所有元素。尤其是对于那些异世界轻改小说爱好者，可以说是强烈推荐了。 硬说细节的话，全部玩下来有几点不是很满意 1.这游戏对魔武双修的BUILD不是很友好，职业虽然多，但是成长物理和魔法分得太明显了，技能伤害计算单调，物理系职业想用魔法技能，伤害幽默； 2.和同伴下本如果同伴被怪打死不管怎样都掉好感，这个在好感初期可以理解，但是好感都已经很高了，还是会掉就有点影响氛围了； 3，装备锻造的等级应该根据目前等级加以限制。不然只要把锻造等级练上去，可以做出远超目前等级水平的装备，直接装备等级碾压。如果不做自我限制，很容易失去打怪乐趣。 当然以上只是对开发者的建议。这游戏如果有什么不会的，直接讨论区发贴就行，不管你用哪种语言，都会有人耐心解答，真是很不错的售后体验。
作为elona代餐也是极好的，虽然简单了很多但是爽点都是一样的，倒不如说简化了以后更容易上手学习成本低也有好处。 在elin出来以后作对比来看更确定一些，虽然上限也因为系统简单了不算太高，希望有持续的更新补充新内容。

Overall, it's very interesting to play. I like the freedom this game provides, with all the possibilities within character interaction, town-building, and randomized world generation. The custom contents are also quite interesting in my opinion. I do wish that in future versions, we could experience more diverse post-final boss content instead of having to reload the save file and play from level 29. Even if it's just some simple change in character speech and the ability to play with the sky island defeated, it will give more fulfillment for completing the main plot with the additional immersion.
